metadata.title: The Engine That Says No.
metadata.purpose: A viewer with no physics or coding background can explain what a closure check is, name the three ways a plan fails it, and say why an engine that declines honestly is more trustworthy than one that always answers — and when declining was itself a bug.

beats.new_visual_element: Claude composer — the ask lands answered
beats.narration_text: Hey, this is Param Madan, and this explainer video is on the closure check: the moment the physics engine decides whether it can answer at all. Here's a surprising result. The team ran the engine on sixty real benchmark problems. It got zero wrong. Because it declined nearly all of them.

props.command: The physics engine got zero wrong on 60 benchmark problems by declining most of them. Is that a good thing?
output: It checks closure before solving anything
A failed check stops, says why, and logs the gap
Declining honestly beats a confident guess

beats.narration_text: In the next few minutes, you'll see three things. First, what closure means, and how the engine checks it. Second, the three ways a plan can fail, and what happens next. And third, why declining honestly beats guessing, and the time declining was itself the bug. No physics or coding background needed.

beats.new_visual_element: can the equations pin it down?
beats.narration_text: The answer up front. Closure means: with what we're given, can the equations pin down every unknown? The engine checks this before it solves anything. If yes, it solves. If no, it stops, says why, and hands the problem on, clearly marked as not verified. It never fills the gap with a guess.

A plan can fail closure in three ways, and each one has a name. First, missing knowns. The card needs a spring constant, and the problem never gave one. Second, the solver itself raises an error. Third, the equations don't resolve to a definite answer. The reason is recorded every time, so a failure points straight at what to fix.

beats.new_visual_element: the damped oscillator goes to the queue
beats.narration_text: Here's what that looks like. The team gave the engine a damped oscillator: a spring whose bouncing slowly dies away. No card covers it. Instead of reaching for the nearest formula, the engine marked it unverified, and logged it as a coverage gap. That log becomes the to-do list for the next card.

Then the real test. On sixty UGPhysics problems, the engine produced zero wrong answers. It also declined nearly everything, because the library is still thin, and most of the benchmark asks for derivations, not numbers. Zero wrong sounds great. But here, it mostly measures honesty, not coverage.

And sometimes declining was the bug. Most of those problems are written in symbols. SymPy can solve those. But the pipeline insisted on turning every answer into a decimal at the very end, so it declined problems it could actually solve. In the team's words, an interface limitation was being reported as a coverage gap. That's worse than an honest gap, because it hid what the engine could already do.

Saying no matters most in grading. If no card produces a verified answer, grade mode returns not assessable, and sends the work to a human. It will not mark a student wrong against an answer it can't verify. And that refusal isn't just a habit. It's a test that runs automatically on the code.

beats.new_visual_element: a tool that is allowed to say no
beats.narration_text: So here's the takeaway. An answer you can trust comes from a tool that's allowed to say, I can't. When an A.I. model gives you an answer, ask whether it could have said no. If it never says no, treat every answer as a guess until you've checked it.
Your turn. Paste this into Claude with a problem you're unsure about. It asks Claude to check closure first, before solving anything.

props.command: Here is a physics problem: [paste it]. Before solving, do a closure check: list every quantity you need, mark each as given or missing, and say whether the equations can pin down the unknowns. If anything is missing, stop and tell me what. Do not assume a value.
output: Every needed quantity: given or missing
Can the equations pin it down?

beats.new_visual_element: title restate, terracotta period, name beneath
beats.narration_text: Check closure. Then solve. This has been Param Madan. Thanks for watching.
